clue.text: Toothy Tom from Tarpoley, perhaps

parts.note: a grinning male cat from a town in the north-western English county whose famous feline grins in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A local man with prominent teeth from a Cheshire market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarporley (printed here as 'Tarpoley') is a town in Cheshire, and a tom is a male cat; Lewis Carroll's grinning cat is the toothy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's feline in Alice is famous for a broad grin, and a tom is a male of its kind, placed by county.

clue.text: Accomplished, like Lancelot Brown in the garden

definitions.text: like Lancelot Brown in the garden
definitions.meaning: the landscape gardener Lancelot Brown was nicknamed 'Capability', so in gardens he showed that quality

explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished means competent; Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape designer, was known by the nickname 'Capability'.

clue.text: Striking effect of someone clattering about

indicators.note: the letters lie about, that is around within, the run of the words someone clattering

explanation.surface: A noisy person banging around makes quite an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means within, so the answer is found spanning 'someonE CLATtering'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for brilliant success or a dazzling show, the impact that strikes onlookers.

clue.text: Iran is hot, but changeable, for a recorder

indicators.note: changeable says the letters of the preceding words are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A comment on Iran's fickle weather, offered for the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changeable' rearranges IRAN IS HOT; 'for a' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: One who writes down and keeps account of past events is a chronicler of the record.

clue.text: Clothes that are fun for students

definitions.meaning: tattered garments, or informally any clothing
British universities hold an annual charity carnival week run by undergraduates, called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Old tatty garments are slang for clothes; a student rag is a British university's charity fundraising event of stunts and parades.

clue.text: He throws his objects, involving rats and mice

indicators.note: involving suggests the words are tangled together, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone hurling things at vermin around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws' looks violent, but a potter throws clay on a wheel; 'involving' mixes up RATS and MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter shapes pots on a wheel, which is called throwing them.

clue.text: Blake's regular, bright night-burner?

parts.note: recalls William Blake's poem about a big cat 'burning bright, in the forests of the night'

explanation.definitionFit: Blake's famous poem pictures this striped big cat burning bright in the forests of the night.

clue.text: Black stuff for nearly all paths, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged in another way
nearly means the word all is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Tarmac is used for almost every footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ALL to AL; 'perhaps' then rearranges AL with PATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark bituminous surfacing used on roads is a black, tarry material.

clue.text: Needs, we hear, wise man in service

definitions.note: the definition is a sound-alike: needs said aloud is kneads, to work muscles with the hands

indicators.note: in places the wise man inside the church service

parts.note: Mass is a church service
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise man attending church because he needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like 'kneads': to knead is to rub and press muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead the body's muscles is to rub and work them, which sounds the same as the clue word.

clue.text: Sweetener given to fortune-teller?

definitions.meaning: a sugar made from the sap of a tropical tree
a fortune-teller reads the hand, so a sweetener for her is sugar for the palm

explanation.definitionFit: It is a sugar from palm-tree sap; a fortune-teller's palm is crossed with silver, so a payment is a sweetener for the hand.

clue.text: G-grind clutch

parts.note: to rasp is to grind or scrape

explanation.surface: A stammered complaint about a grinding car clutch.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'G-grind' supplies a lone G before RASP.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch something is to seize it tightly in the hand.

clue.text: Weaver who can move in one direction only!

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: who can move in one direction only!
definitions.meaning: from the lowest point the only way to go is up

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream bears this name; at the lowest point, the only way is upward.

clue.text: A doctor ordered fresh air, so, and very best food

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: the letters are freshly ordered, put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A physician prescribes fresh air and the finest meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a doctor's prescription; 'ordered fresh' is the anagram signal, applied only to 'air, so'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth it was the food of the gods, so anything supremely delicious.

clue.text: Dulcie bad in geometry

indicators.note: bad suggests the name is spoilt, its letters disordered

explanation.surface: A girl called Dulcie is poor at maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges DULCIE; the definition is loose, naming the Greek mathematician who is the great name in that subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek mathematician whose Elements founded the study of plane figures.

clue.text: Wise or Wisdom?

parts.note: Ernie Wise and Norman Wisdom were both British funny men of stage and screen

explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise and Norman Wisdom were famous British comic performers, so either is an example.

clue.text: No fast food, this!

parts.note: a dish of snails, the slowest of creatures, so not quick food

explanation.definitionFit: Snails served as a French dish; the snail is proverbially slow, so not fast in either sense.

clue.text: Are those on it calling taxmen "Sir", perhaps?

definitions.text: Are those on it calling taxmen "Sir", perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asks whether people being reprimanded are being polite to tax inspectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TAXMEN SIR; someone 'on the carpet' is being reprimanded, and an Axminster is a carpet, so the whole clue pictures it.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of woven carpet, named after a Devon town, which people stand on.

clue.text: Signs of vitamin deficiency? Try this double Brie-spread

indicators.note: spread says the letters are scattered into a new order
double says the cheese name is taken two times over

explanation.surface: A suggestion that eating lots of cheese will cure a dietary illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives BRIEBRIE, which 'spread' rearranges; 'Try this' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease caused by lack of thiamine, vitamin B1, showing as nerve and heart symptoms.

clue.text: Moon dies away and masks appear

indicators.note: away suggests the letters drift off out of their order

explanation.surface: As the moon fades, masked figures emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges MOON DIES; 'appear' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a hooded cloak with a half-face covering worn at masquerades.

clue.text: Takes twice the time to make old tunic

parts.note: to double something is to take it twice

explanation.surface: A slow tailor needs twice as long to sew an antique garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting man's jacket worn in Renaissance Europe, as with hose.

clue.text: Absorbs half day benefits

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning half of the day
uses are benefits or advantages

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a half-day holiday's perks.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to occupy the attention, as something absorbing does.

clue.text: What a heavenly colour!

parts.note: heavenly read literally, the shade of the sky above

explanation.definitionFit: The pale azure of a clear daytime sky; 'heavenly' means of the heavens.

clue.text: Too little for a lot

parts.note: a lot is an item at auction, and offering too little for it is an insufficient offer

explanation.definitionFit: An offer below value at auction, or a too-low call in bridge.

clue.text: Father leaves town near Glasgow for refit

indicators.note: leaves means the father departs from the town's name, taken out of it

parts.note: Renfrew is a town west of Glasgow in Scotland
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A priest moves from a Scottish town for a fresh fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking FR out of RENFREW leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit something is to restore or replace it, to make it new again.

clue.text: As apprehensive as a crowned head?

definitions.text: As apprehensive as a crowned head?

parts.words: As apprehensive as a crowned head?
parts.note: recalls Shakespeare's line in Henry IV Part 2 about the restlessness of the head that wears a crown

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote that the head that wears a crown lies anxious and restless.

clue.text: Terrier with no drink is taken for a walk

indicators.note: with no says the drink is removed from the dog breed

parts.note: an Airedale is a breed of terrier
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A thirsty dog is led out for exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: AIREDALE without ALE leaves the answer; a dog that is 'aired' has been given an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a dog is to give it an outing in the fresh air.

clue.text: A damson's place at hospital?

parts.note: to set is to place

explanation.surface: Wondering where a plum belongs in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, 'A damson' reads 'Adam's son': in the Bible Seth is the third son of Adam; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Seth is the third son born to Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Master and king by name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A king called by his title.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to acquire it by study.

clue.text: Sort of roll, A-E, etc.?

indicators.note: sort, as a verb, says the letters that follow are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A register listing names alphabetically from A to E and onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges ROLL, A, E and ETC; a voters' register is listed alphabetically, A–E and so on, so the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: The register of voters is a list of names, kept in alphabetical order.

clue.text: Contemplate game of cards on a big scale

parts.note: to weigh up is to contemplate
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Thinking about card games played in a grand way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a big scale' looks like 'largely', but a weighbridge is a big weighing machine for lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform machine for weighing vehicles, a very large weighing device.
